failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Some communities show readable spacing and hierarchy, but repeated card shells and templated status copy in Camera Club, Member Social Space, Ad-Free Community, and Data Portability keep the UI below a modern shippable product bar.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does this feel like a rich product experience for the community and persona rather than an implementation workflow surface?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Garden Club, Book Club, HOA, and parts of Masjid Nur show concrete community content, but several personas still see generic task cards rather than full product flows such as a real thread, checkout, ad-off entitlement, gear loan, or export console.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the information architecture centered on real community content and jobs-to-be-done?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The app often groups screens around domain sections, but whole areas are still organized as repeated workflow/state surfaces with labels like Current state, Status notice, Result visible, Restore path, and Local package details instead of navigable community content and jobs-to-be-done.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Are primary surfaces domain-native rather than repeated workflow cards?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Screenshots still show repeated primary card surfaces across unrelated workflows: the same icon, title, summary, status chips, current-state panel, saved/result panel, and bottom support section recur across camera, platform social, ad-off, and export flows.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does the screen provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Concrete content and actions are visible in many rows, but 26 workflow/persona paths still lack convincing lifecycle closure from pixels: alternate/change/reject affordances, persistent receipt/result, receiver or continuation states, or task-specific decision data are missing or generic.

tickets.workerReadiness: no concrete implementation work item was generated; planner must inspect the direct-question failure before assigning a worker
tickets.firstRequiredStep: Review failing direct questions and add screen/workflow/persona-specific evidence before implementation.
implementationBlockedBy: The ticket lacks row-level implementation evidence.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Some communities show readable spacing and hierarchy, but repeated card shells and templated status copy in Camera Club, Member Social Space, Ad-Free Community, and Data Portability keep the UI below a modern shippable product bar.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does this feel like a rich product experience for the community and persona rather than an implementation workflow surface?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Garden Club, Book Club, HOA, and parts of Masjid Nur show concrete community content, but several personas still see generic task cards rather than full product flows such as a real thread, checkout, ad-off entitlement, gear loan, or export console.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the information architecture centered on real community content and jobs-to-be-done?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The app often groups screens around domain sections, but whole areas are still organized as repeated workflow/state surfaces with labels like Current state, Status notice, Result visible, Restore path, and Local package details instead of navigable community content and jobs-to-be-done.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Are primary surfaces domain-native rather than repeated workflow cards?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Screenshots still show repeated primary card surfaces across unrelated workflows: the same icon, title, summary, status chips, current-state panel, saved/result panel, and bottom support section recur across camera, platform social, ad-off, and export flows.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does the screen provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Concrete content and actions are visible in many rows, but 26 workflow/persona paths still lack convincing lifecycle closure from pixels: alternate/change/reject affordances, persistent receipt/result, receiver or continuation states, or task-specific decision data are missing or generic.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Some communities show readable spacing and hierarchy, but repeated card shells and templated status copy in Camera Club, Member Social Space, Ad-Free Community, and Data Portability keep the UI below a modern shippable product bar.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does this feel like a rich product experience for the community and persona rather than an implementation workflow surface?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Garden Club, Book Club, HOA, and parts of Masjid Nur show concrete community content, but several personas still see generic task cards rather than full product flows such as a real thread, checkout, ad-off entitlement, gear loan, or export console.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the information architecture centered on real community content and jobs-to-be-done?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The app often groups screens around domain sections, but whole areas are still organized as repeated workflow/state surfaces with labels like Current state, Status notice, Result visible, Restore path, and Local package details instead of navigable community content and jobs-to-be-done.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Are primary surfaces domain-native rather than repeated workflow cards?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Screenshots still show repeated primary card surfaces across unrelated workflows: the same icon, title, summary, status chips, current-state panel, saved/result panel, and bottom support section recur across camera, platform social, ad-off, and export flows.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does the screen provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Concrete content and actions are visible in many rows, but 26 workflow/persona paths still lack convincing lifecycle closure from pixels: alternate/change/reject affordances, persistent receipt/result, receiver or continuation states, or task-specific decision data are missing or generic.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Some communities show readable spacing and hierarchy, but repeated card shells and templated status copy in Camera Club, Member Social Space, Ad-Free Community, and Data Portability keep the UI below a modern shippable product bar.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does this feel like a rich product experience for the community and persona rather than an implementation workflow surface?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Garden Club, Book Club, HOA, and parts of Masjid Nur show concrete community content, but several personas still see generic task cards rather than full product flows such as a real thread, checkout, ad-off entitlement, gear loan, or export console.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the information architecture centered on real community content and jobs-to-be-done?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The app often groups screens around domain sections, but whole areas are still organized as repeated workflow/state surfaces with labels like Current state, Status notice, Result visible, Restore path, and Local package details instead of navigable community content and jobs-to-be-done.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Are primary surfaces domain-native rather than repeated workflow cards?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Screenshots still show repeated primary card surfaces across unrelated workflows: the same icon, title, summary, status chips, current-state panel, saved/result panel, and bottom support section recur across camera, platform social, ad-off, and export flows.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does the screen provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Concrete content and actions are visible in many rows, but 26 workflow/persona paths still lack convincing lifecycle closure from pixels: alternate/change/reject affordances, persistent receipt/result, receiver or continuation states, or task-specific decision data are missing or generic.

tickets.problemStatement: The evidence does not prove that each workflow/persona UI implements the full production lifecycle. Cards may expose a single accept/cancel action without the decision context, alternate choices, result state, or receiver/continuation state real users need.
tickets.rootCauseHypothesis: The product experience was modeled as completed workflows rather than lifecycle-complete user tasks, so the UI can appear polished while still missing required fields, negative/change actions, and durable post-action states.
tickets.targetExperience: Each workflow/persona surface should show the concrete object, decision information, natural primary and alternate actions, persistent result/receipt/status, and receiver/continuation state expected in a production app.
uxPrinciples: Workflows are product lifecycles, not one-shot checklist actions
Users need enough information to decide before acting
Production affordances include alternate choices, change/revoke paths, and clear result states when the domain requires them
Receiver and continuation states are first-class UX, not hidden backend assertions

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Some communities show readable spacing and hierarchy, but repeated card shells and templated status copy in Camera Club, Member Social Space, Ad-Free Community, and Data Portability keep the UI below a modern shippable product bar.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does this feel like a rich product experience for the community and persona rather than an implementation workflow surface?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Garden Club, Book Club, HOA, and parts of Masjid Nur show concrete community content, but several personas still see generic task cards rather than full product flows such as a real thread, checkout, ad-off entitlement, gear loan, or export console.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the information architecture centered on real community content and jobs-to-be-done?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The app often groups screens around domain sections, but whole areas are still organized as repeated workflow/state surfaces with labels like Current state, Status notice, Result visible, Restore path, and Local package details instead of navigable community content and jobs-to-be-done.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Are primary surfaces domain-native rather than repeated workflow cards?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Screenshots still show repeated primary card surfaces across unrelated workflows: the same icon, title, summary, status chips, current-state panel, saved/result panel, and bottom support section recur across camera, platform social, ad-off, and export flows.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does the screen provide concrete content and lifecycle actions a real user needs?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Concrete content and actions are visible in many rows, but 26 workflow/persona paths still lack convincing lifecycle closure from pixels: alternate/change/reject affordances, persistent receipt/result, receiver or continuation states, or task-specific decision data are missing or generic.
